questions.question: What is the primary purpose and origin of the R programming language?
options: It is a database management system created by Oracle in 1985
It is a programming language designed specifically for statistical computing, data analysis, and visualization, created by Ross Ihaka and Robert Gentleman in 1993
It is a styling language created by Microsoft for browser user interfaces
It is an operating system kernel developed by Bell Labs
questions.hint: Think of the two statisticians at the University of Auckland whose first names both start with 'R'.
questions.explanation: R was developed in 1993 by Ross Ihaka and Robert Gentleman at the University of Auckland, New Zealand. It is an open-source implementation of the S language, built specifically for data analysis, statistical modeling, and graphical visualization.

questions.question: What is the key difference between R and RStudio?
options: R is an IDE while RStudio is a database driver
R is the actual programming language engine, while RStudio is an Integrated Development Environment (IDE) that provides a convenient graphical interface to write and run R code
RStudio is the programming language that completely replaces R
R and RStudio are identical terms for the exact same software
questions.hint: Remember the car engine versus dashboard controls analogy.
questions.explanation: R is the core programming language and computation engine. RStudio is a feature-rich IDE (Integrated Development Environment) developed by Posit that provides source editing, plotting windows, an environment viewer, and a console to make R development productive.

questions.question: What is CRAN in the R ecosystem?
options: A proprietary cloud hosting company that charges monthly fees for R code
The Comprehensive R Archive Network — the official central network of mirrors that hosts the R installer, source code, and thousands of verified community packages
A graphics card driver required to draw bar charts in R
A hardware chip built into statistical laboratory machines
questions.hint: Look for the acronym that stands for Comprehensive R Archive Network.
questions.explanation: CRAN (Comprehensive R Archive Network) is the primary distribution network for R. It stores official binary installers, documentation manuals, and over 20,000 tested open-source packages created by the global R community.

questions.question: Why does the R console display '[1]' before outputting the result of '10 + 20'?
options: It means there is only 1 second remaining before R shuts down
It indicates that the line printed starts with the first (index 1) element of the resulting vector
It represents a syntax error warning code
It shows that the computation took 1 byte of RAM
questions.hint: In R, even single numbers are stored as vectors starting at index 1.
questions.explanation: In R, individual numbers are 1-element vectors. The prefix '[1]' indicates that the first item displayed on that output row corresponds to index 1 of the output vector.

questions.question: What file extension is universally used for saving R scripts?
options: .rscript
.R (or .r)
.rdata
.rmd
questions.hint: It is a single letter matching the language's name.
questions.explanation: R scripts containing plain text source code are saved with the '.R' (or '.r') file extension, allowing RStudio and command-line runners to recognize and execute them.

questions.question: When setting up your development environment on Windows, in what order should you install the software?
options: Install RStudio first, and never install base R
Install Base R first from CRAN, and then install RStudio Desktop from Posit
Install Python first, then RStudio, and then delete base R
RStudio must be installed on a USB flash drive only
questions.hint: The dashboard needs an engine to connect to.
questions.explanation: You must install Base R from CRAN first so that RStudio can detect the existing R binary and runtime libraries when it launches.

questions.question: Which of the following compares R, Python, and SQL accurately?
options: SQL is designed for machine learning, Python is only for math, and R is for database management

R specializes in statistical data analysis and publication-grade charts, Python is a general-purpose programming language widely used in AI/web, and SQL is specialized for querying relational databases
R and Python cannot be used together in modern data science
R has no visualization capabilities whatsoever
questions.hint: Each language has a distinct core strength in data science.
questions.explanation: R is optimized for statistical computing and visualization, Python excels across general programming and machine learning, and SQL manages and queries relational database tables. They frequently work together in professional data pipelines.

questions.question: Which character is used to write single-line comments in R?
questions.hint: The same character used for hashtags in social media.
questions.explanation: In R, the hash symbol '#' introduces a single-line comment. Everything from the '#' to the end of the line is ignored by the R interpreter.

questions.question: How can a beginner access the official built-in documentation for the 'print' function directly inside the R console?
options: search(print)
?print or help(print)
docs -> print
man print
questions.hint: You can prepend a question mark to the function name.
questions.explanation: Typing '?print' or 'help(print)' in the R console opens the official help documentation describing the function's arguments, description, and usage examples.

questions.question: What is 'Rscript' and what is its primary utility?
options: A commercial plugin that must be purchased separately
A command-line executable bundled with R that runs an R script file directly from the terminal without opening an interactive GUI
A web browser extension for reading R files
A text editor designed exclusively for macOS
questions.hint: It allows batch script execution in automated pipelines (e.g., Rscript script.R).
questions.explanation: 'Rscript' is a standalone command-line tool included with R that executes R scripts in batch or non-interactive mode (e.g. 'Rscript analysis.R'), making it ideal for scheduled tasks and automated pipelines.
